title: Convert Folder
paragraphs: “So… according to Motoyasu, it seems that after Itsuki—which was the condition for the loop—died, Motoyasu returned to this loop, and it’s been continuing ever since.”
Father also explained that, in order to eliminate the remnants of Takt using Shieldfreeden, he would have to command a dragon. So, I’ve explained the entire current situation.
“I see… I’ve got a general grasp of the situation.”
“According to Motoyasu, this is apparently the second time the loop has restarted.”
“So the first time, he didn’t even get close to the dragon?”
“Of course not.”
“That Spear Hero is still such an idiot…”
“What did you say?!”
That dragon is as combative as ever. I could send you to the afterlife with a single thrust!
“I can’t deny that…”
“Yeah, I guess so.”
“No doubt about it… Of course, I do believe Lord Kitamura himself is taking this seriously…”
Panda and Éclair both agree. Whose side are you guys on, anyway!?
“I get it now. If it’s a request from Naofumi, I’ll be happy to help.”
“That’d be a big help.”
“But… Gaelion, I’d rather not have Naofumi look after me until I’ve leveled up and fully matured.”
“Huh? Why?”
“Because if I do, Naofumi will see Gaelion as a child.”
“Hahahahaha!　You’ve finally shown your true colors! This one is a total predator through and through. Father! You’d better watch out!”
She’s started making blatant sexual advances toward Father. That’s backfiring! Then Rival looks at me with pitying eyes before turning her gaze back to Father.
“Even though this is the first body he’s gotten used to, Gaelion has still lived through countless loops and a long, wild time in Ofumi’s world. Being treated like a child hurts a dragon’s pride.”
Hmm… It’s all in how you say it! To begin with, you just said you hadn’t updated your memories much! That’s a contradiction!
When was your last memory update, anyway!? You said you became a Raph… Do you actually have a memory of that? I can vaguely make out a silhouette that looks like it, but I must be mistaken.
“You were in that chocolate form for a long time, weren’t you!”
“Ah, that brings back memories. That body was so comfortable.”
“Um, I kind of get that Gaelion-chan is older.”
“That’s right.”
That’s definitely a lie! Don’t let her fool you!
“Well, I guess so. Since you’re stuck in a loop and still have your memories, it’s only natural that your appearance and mental age wouldn’t match.”
“I think there are exceptions, though…”
Éclair is bringing up some kind of exception to Father’s opinion.
“…You’d better just let it go. It must be tough to repeat the same time over and over again unless you have a mind that strong.”
“R-right…”

Father and Éclair seem to be on the same page. Ugh… For some reason, Rival’s standing is rising. I’ve looped through time far more times than he has, so I’ve lived much longer. That means I should be mentally stronger!
“Dragons are practically immortal! You’ll always be a kid, Father!”

“Yeah, that’s true… But still, Gaelion-chan. Technically, I’m the one who’ll be raising you, right? Motoyasu-kun and Sakura-chan would probably hate it, and since I want you to become just as strong as Lars-chan and the others in preparation for the coming battle, I’d like to raise you myself.”
HAHAHA. My plan’s already fallen apart. That’s why dragons are useless!
“…I guess I have no choice. But please don’t treat me like a kid.”
“Got it. So should I call you Gaelion-san? It feels a little off, though.”
“‘-chan’ is better! I hate being treated like an old person.”
“You don’t want to be treated like a kid, but you don’t want to be treated like an old person either… That’s a tough one.”
“That’s just how dragons are!”
I must say, you have a wildly complicated mental makeup. Compared to that, Filolial-sama and the others possess eternal purity! As expected, Filolial-sama is a far more wonderful being than a dragon.
“So, Gaelion-chan, do you remember how to break through the limit?”
“Of course I do. I’ve saved it as a memory, so as long as I have the minimum amount of Core Stones and a Hero’s weapon, I can do it.”
“That’s a huge help. Well then, I’m counting on you from now on, Gaelion-chan.”
Although she’s not happy about it, our Rival has officially joined the party. From now on, you’d better work like a workhorse and contribute to Father.

“Of course I will. I’ll do my best to get Shieldfreeden to accept Naofumi and the others! Since I gathered Core Stones from the Dragon Emperor—who was even called the Demon King in another world—to grow stronger, I know all sorts of other things and Magic, too. I’m a powered-up Gaelion who can even govern!”
That’s the sort of thing Rival is going on about. She really is a noisy one.
“You seem reliable. By the way, things have pretty much come together now… but, um, I kind of dragged you out here against your will—what about your Older Sister…?”
“Oh, she’s fine. I’ll go back home when I have time. It’s only natural to support my family. Gaelion, I’m a ‘dispatched dragon.’”
“Dispatched…? You seem to know quite a lot about all sorts of things…”

Father looks utterly dumbfounded at Rival’s self-sabotage. Heh heh heh… Judging by that look, winning Father’s heart is nothing but a pipe dream. Go ahead and dig your own grave even more pathetically.
“That’s right, Rival.”
“What is it? Spear Hero, what’s up?”
“I’m going to analyze your looping function, kick it out, and turn it into Filo-chan’s convert folder, so give me a hand, okay?”
“…What are you talking about?”
Rival looked completely bewildered. What are you spacing out for? Hurry up and convert Filo-chan! Do it!
“Motoyasu-kun, you’re still terrible at explaining things…”
“Yeah, you are.”
“That’s right.”
“Yeah.”
So all three of you Knights—don’t go agreeing in unison like Ren and Itsuki! Anyway, hurry up and make Filo-tan’s memories eternal!

“Um, in this world, the Filolial Motoyasu-kun was after ended up being Sakura-chan, right? But since Motoyasu-kun can’t quite give up, he wants to—like he did with Gaelion-chan—help Sakura-chan recall the memories of a girl named Filo? That’s what he wants to do.”
“So, kick Gaelion out and be with Filo? I don’t think Filo would be able to handle that.”
"After all, Filo is a divine, transparent being, just like glass. But I won't give up. Rival, it's about time you got out of the spear and gave that space to Filo."

“Spear Hero… The reason Gaelion can ride the loop is because he possesses immortality—a physiology that allows his consciousness and memories to be contained within the Core Stone. Filolials don’t have that kind of physiology.”
With a deadpan expression, Rival is giving me a pitying look. What’s that supposed to mean? Don’t be ridiculous!
“There is a Filolial Queen with eternal life, but she’s from a different lineage, so it’s impossible. Give it up.”
Ugh… So does that mean the ‘Filo-chan Eternal’ plan has failed? Then, why on earth did I resurrect Rival? No, it’s too early to give up!
“I won’t give up! I’m going to use your space to carry out the Eternal Filo-tan Project! That’s why I’m going to erase your memories from inside the spear and create a Filo-tan folder!”
After all, I managed to create a dragon-like creature. With Filolial-sama’s sacred and indomitable power, I’m sure we can make it happen. Filo-chan, foreverrrrr!
“This kind of feels like you’re declaring you’re going to kill me right in front of me…”
“Don’t worry about it. The Spear Hero is just the same as always. Anyway, what can’t be done can’t be done. Since it’s impossible the Gaelion way, you’d better look for another method.”
“You’re not saying it can’t be done, are you?”
“It’s just sympathy. Since Filo used to be the Hero of the Claws, why not have her wield a weapon from the Ryukoku series—one that’s apparently malfunctioning somewhere—in some loop or another?”
Rival is looking at me with pity for some reason! It’s pointless to try to score points with Father by giving me that look! This is my ambition, after all!
“I think we should figure out why the loop is restarting in the first place.”
“That’s true, but… do you know, Gaelion-chan?”
“I need to get a little stronger before I can interfere with the spear. Right now, Gaelion has only inherited the memories.”
“I see. Well, then, we’ll have to work hard from here on out to get things done.”
“It’s getting noisy again, isn’t it?”
“It’s getting livelier and livelier, isn’t it?”
“Nice to meet you.”
Each of them addressed Rival. That Rival then said to the panda:
“Speaking of which, you’re the Dressed-Up Panda, aren’t you? How did you end up with Naofumi in this world?”
“Huh!? Who said I’m ‘Dressed-Up’!?”
The panda’s veins bulged as he yelled at Rival.
“In Wild Naofumi’s world, Gaelion doesn’t remember anyone other than the ‘Dressed-Up Panda’ who was called Sasa-chan.”
Hearing that name, the panda’s fur bristled just like before.
“So what’s that name supposed to mean!?”
“Pfft… Sasa, huh? I guess you could call her that.”
“Elmero! Youuuuuu!”
The panda looked at Rival, then pointed at the elephant. The one who’d called him “Sasa-chan” was his Older Sister.
“I don’t know. Oh, but the female knight next to her was often seen with the Sword Hero.”
“Me? Well, given the phenomenon of loops, there might be some connection there. So you, like Lord Kitamura, are someone who’s been repeating this cycle, aren’t you?”
“That’s right. There might be some things about me that you find a bit creepy, but I look forward to getting to know you.”
“I wouldn’t dislike you for something like that. I look forward to getting to know you as well.”
“Well then, let’s keep the introductions brief and start figuring out what to do next.”
And that’s how time passed.

For now, Father and the others returned to Siltvelt and decided to level up. Meanwhile, I’ll be traveling around the various regions to slay dragons. This was not only to boost Rival’s abilities but also to increase my own Limit Break power. The goal was to create an elite force capable of taking down the hidden Takt faction more swiftly.
“Well… now that we’ve decided on a plan, would it be okay if we did a little sparring to coordinate our future teamwork?”
Éclair asked Panda and Zou.
“After all, we’ll have to level up with Lord Iwatani without the assistance of Lord Kitamura or the Filolials. I believe we need to share what we can do to make that happen.”
“That makes sense, but revealing our strategies is a bit scary, isn’t it? Even though we’re a friendly faction with a proven track record, you’re still a knight of Melromarc, right?”
“Hm?”
Éclair raised an eyebrow at Panda’s discriminatory remark. But knowing Éclair, I don’t think she meant anything by it—she was simply asking for information sharing.
“Lars-chan, Eclair isn’t that kind of person. She’s incredibly serious.”
“Yeah, yeah. So she’s a stiff-necked knight and a military type, is she? Either way, when it comes to humans—except for a select few—they’re generally mediocre, so I’d like to see what you’ve got.”
“Ah, well then, let’s have a sparring match. I’ve been looking forward to this.”

“What kind of warrior race are you guys, anyway?” That’s exactly what Father from the first world would have said. Not just Éclair, but there were plenty of guys like this among the old woman’s disciples.
“Don’t try to hide your snarling face, okay?”
Éclair drew her sword, and Panda bared her claws and took a fighting stance.
“Alright, let’s settle this at the castle’s training ground.”
“Lasa!”
“Elmero, you’re in too! Or are we just a bunch of women who swarm around the Shield Hero? We’ve got to show what we’re made of right here and now.”
Hoho, that’s a pretty good line coming from a panda. Wanting to contribute rather than just leech off Father… I guess I need to rethink my opinion of Panda.
“…I see. I get the logic. But do we really have to do this right here?”

“It’s precisely because it’s just beginning. To begin with, I don’t think the Shield Hero even has a clue how strong we really are. He probably just has a vague sense that we’re stronger than the average guy around here.”
Panda glances at Father once before turning her attention to Zou.
“Honestly, I couldn’t care less. What about you? You’re acting so out of character. Did you really want to play knight that badly?”
“W-well, I…”
“Either way, I think this is a good opportunity. We just need to let Lord Iwatani and the others see what we’re capable of. I’d also like to spar with you later.”
“Since we’re about to face the waves,” Éclair continued. Then, as if in perfect unison, she and Panda set off toward the training grounds.
